strategy.summary: MatrixFrac._grad in cvxpy computes the gradient w.r.t. a matrix X with DX.T.ravel(order='F'), which equals row-major flattening and gives wrong gradients when X has more than one column. The fix removes the .T so the gradient is vectorized column-major. Reproduce by running the regression test matrix_frac_matrix_x (X shape (3,2), P psd (3,3)) through the Atom.grad finite-difference check in cvxpy/tests/test_grad.py; it must fail on b5a20484ff95 and pass after the fix.

pip_packages: cvxpy (checkout of buggy commit b5a20484ff95 installed in editable mode: pip install -e .)
pinned_because: Dependency floors are documented in the README (kind: explicit, era_ceiling null), so the minimums listed are the documented constraints and are used as-is; no era-inferred pins were added.
No C/C++ compilation is required for the Python-level gradient path under test, so needs_build is false.

strategy.reproducing_test: cvxpy/tests/test_grad.py MultiVarAtomConfig entry 'matrix_frac_matrix_x': cp.matrix_frac(x, P) with x unrestricted of shape (3,2) and P psd of shape (3,3), checked by comparing Atom.grad against a finite-difference gradient.
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy revision b5a20484ff95 the matrix_frac_matrix_x case fails because the Atom.grad gradient w.r.t. X (computed via DX.T.ravel(order='F'), i.e. row-major) disagrees with the finite-difference reference by up to roughly 0.97, so the assertion trips. On the fixed revision, where the line is DX.ravel(order='F'), the same case passes with max finite-difference error around 1.85e-08. The transition fail-to-pass is the whole criterion.
strategy.numerical_probe: Compare Atom.grad of matrix_frac(X,P) with X of shape (3,2) against central finite differences of tr(X^T P^-1 X); the gradient should be (P^-1+P^-T)X in column-major order.

input_output_examples.input: matrix_frac with matrix X of shape (n, p), p > 1; Atom.grad call
input_output_examples.buggy_output: gradient with errors up to ~0.97 relative to finite-difference check
input_output_examples.expected_output: gradient matching finite-difference check with max error ~1.85e-08

risks: Bug only appears for matrix X with more than one column; a vector-X test will not transition, so the (3,2) shape in matrix_frac_matrix_x is essential.
Must exercise Atom.grad directly; problem.backward() and problem.derivative() use diffcp and bypass the faulty _grad path, so they will not show the failure.

The test relies on the finite-difference helper in test_grad.py; if that helper's tolerance is loose the buggy error could be masked, so confirm the assertion tolerance actually separates ~0.97 from ~1e-8.
Dependency floors (e.g. NumPy 2.x, SciPy 1.13) are documented rather than era-inferred; if the environment resolves older packages the test may fail for unrelated reasons.

oracle.why: The expected gradient is checked against a numerical finite-difference reference; the stated post-fix max error ~1.85e-08 versus ~0.97 before indicates a tolerance-based comparison separating the two.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The Atom.grad result for the (3,2) matrix X is transposed in vectorization order relative to the finite-difference reference, giving errors near 0.97, so the finite-difference assertion for matrix_frac_matrix_x fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: With the .T removed, Atom.grad column-major vectorization matches the finite-difference reference to about 1.85e-08, so the assertion passes.
